references.text: The immediate context: Jesus tells the parable of the friend who comes at midnight and asks for bread, which verse 7 directly responds to.
Jesus explains the point of the parable: even if the friend will not get up out of friendship, he will still rise because of the other's persistence – an encouragement to perseverance in prayer.
The parable of the unjust judge and the widow has the same structure: a reluctant person who eventually gives in to persistent prayer, illustrating the need for perseverance in prayer.
Proverbs warns against saying to your neighbor "Go, come again tomorrow" when you have the opportunity to help now – the same motive as the reluctant friend's refusal.
Matthew's parallel to Jesus' teaching on prayer: "Ask and it will be given to you" – the same context about God's willingness to give to those who ask, in contrast to the reluctant friend.
The Canaanite woman first meets rejection from Jesus, but her perseverance in prayer leads to her receiving what she asked for – a parallel to the theme of persistence in prayer.
Lot insists on hospitality toward the two angels who initially refuse, an example of persistent hospitality that mirrors the situation in Jesus' parable.
In the Song of Songs, the beloved knocks at the door during the night, but she has already gone to bed – a parallel imagery with being woken up at night and reluctance to get up.
